speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: asked the Minister for Law whether the Government will consider (i) adopting a common and universal definition of mental disorder and mental disability across all legislation and (ii) conducting a thorough review on all relevant criminal legislation to incorporate appropriate safeguards, protection and support for persons with mental disorders or mental disabilities who have to interact with the criminal justice system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The first part of the question is whether there can be a common definition of mental disorder and mental disability across different legislation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The issue of one's mental condition arises in many different contexts in the different legislation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: There are provisions that are aimed at protecting persons with mental conditions from abuse.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, section 376F of the Penal Code deals with the procurement of sexual activity with persons with mental disabilities by means of inducement, threat or deception and defines mental disability as, and I quote, "an impairment of or a disturbance in the functioning of the mind or brain resulting from any disability or disorder of the mind or brain which impairs the ability to make a proper judgement in the giving of consent to sexual touching".

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: There are also provisions which deal with the detention of persons with mental conditions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For instance, the Mental Health (Care and Treatment) Act allows the detention of a person who suffers from a mental disorder, where a designated medical practitioner at a psychiatric institution is of the opinion that the person requires in-patient treatment at the psychiatric institution and such detention is necessary in the interests of the person's health or safety, or for the protection of other persons.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: There are also provisions to protect the interests of persons who lack mental capacity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, the Mental Capacity Act addresses the need to make decisions for persons who are 21 years of age or older when they lack mental capacity to make those decisions for themselves.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Under the Act, a person lacks mental capacity in relation to a matter, and I quote, "if at the material time he is unable to make a decision for himself in relation to the matter because of an impairment of, or a disturbance in the functioning of the mind or brain".

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Mental disorders and mental disabilities take many different forms, with different levels of severity and impairment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The different provisions are drafted to deal with the different specific contexts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The second part of the Member's question is about whether we will review all relevant criminal legislation to incorporate appropriate safeguards and support for persons with mental conditions who interact with the criminal justice system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: MHA's response to Question Nos 8, 9, 10 and 11 on the Order Paper for this Sitting will address the safeguards during investigations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: In addition to those, there are procedural protections at the trial stage for witnesses, including those with mental conditions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, the State Courts administer a Witness Support Programme for vulnerable witnesses in criminal cases, such as adults with mental capacity below the age of 18.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: A trained volunteer will be assigned to the vulnerable witness to accompany and provide the emotional support to the witness before, during and also after the hearing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Due regard is also given to the mental conditions of accused persons when they are prosecuted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: For example, the criminal case will not proceed if the accused is found to be of unsound mind and, consequently, incapable of making his defence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: If the accused is capable of making his defence but was of unsound mind at the time he committed the act that he was charged with, the Court must acquit him and report the case to the Minister.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: He may then be confined in a psychiatric institution, with periodic reviews of his state of mind.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The Court may also take into account the offender's mental condition in deciding the appropriate sentence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Of course, as and when we realise or we observe that it can be improved, we will do so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai) (for the Minister for Law)
text: If the Member has any suggestions for improvement, we invite her to share them with us and we will consider.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I think we have moved far along in the mental health and well-being discourse.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I do note that the Minister said there is always continual review for this.
